requirements.text: Step 0: record start revision and pre-existing changes; check /.agents/notes/index.md if present; verify every grounding row against the checkout/environment, record expected versus actual, baseline failing-test identities and the throwaway external-repository worktree child-trust check before production edits. Stop only if a contradiction changes design, outcomes, scope or verification, including trust blocking without a noninteractive route.

Stay within §5 and §6: never change protected spec tests, existing tests except the three §6.6 fixture edits, SPEC-0010, SPEC-0015, duplicate index rows, pi-rework, models/thinking, plan gate, quota semantics, progress protocol/rendering, other repositories' IDs or router package. No new extension, /implement command, main landing, routing suite, guideline or system-prompt instruction. Only the Plan-interface path may change in the planner prompt.

Preserve the required sibling .tests/ directory and delegated route. Record that a full model-driven run in another repository is deferred to the next real use; never substitute an inline implementation or count unrun checks as passes.
lib/specs.ts: recognize SPEC-<ID>-<slug>.md with nonempty [0-9A-Za-z]+ ID; retain slug/file shape, original ID spelling and sorting, and exclude SPEC-<ID>-run.md and non-spec entries.

resolveSpec: accept ID alone or SPEC-prefixed with case-insensitive ID comparison, numeric queries up to four digits with existing zero-padding, filename/path with or without .md, and slug. Preserve all old successful queries, including prefixed short numeric IDs and existing filename-ID resolution.
resolveSpec: more than one hit is an error naming every hit, including case-folded duplicate IDs and ambiguous slugs; keep existing unknown/error wording otherwise.

markImplemented: match exactly one alphanumeric first-cell ID case-insensitively, preserve the exactly-one-row error, whitespace/unrelated cells/header behaviour, set implemented and Implemented by. Preserve all numeric-spec behaviour, specPaths and bin/pi-rework unchanged.
Export STOP_AND_REPORT exactly: Do not implement this spec with other tools. Report this result to the user and wait for instructions.

Export findHarnessRoot(fromPath: string): string | null. Realpath the input, start at it if a directory or at its parent otherwise, return the real nearest ancestor containing bin/pi-implement, and return null on any error or exhaustion. Follow file/directory symlinks; do not require docs/specs.

Export targetRepo(cwd: string): string | null, realpath of git -C cwd rev-parse --show-toplevel, returning null on failure including nonrepositories and missing directories; support subdirectories and worktrees.
implementArgs accepts optional repo?: string and appends --repo, repo after today's spec, --progress json, optional --plan-only, optional --resume arguments; preserve no-repo behaviour.

pythonProjectFor first returns the target .pi/pipeline.json pythonProject when it is a nonempty string, kept relative to the target. This target override wins even when target equals harness and over a target pyproject.toml.

pythonProjectFor fallback order: same-real-path target/harness uses settings.pipeline.pythonProject or tools/map; a foreign target with pyproject.toml uses .; otherwise null. Never leak the harness host Python default into a foreign target.

runDirBase({ runRoot, target, harnessRoot, id, slug }) returns runRoot/SPEC-<id>-<slug> for the harness target, otherwise runRoot/<basename(target)>/SPEC-<id>-<slug>; recognize real-path aliases and preserve the spec tests' lexical nonexistent-path inputs.

Export planPrompt({ spec, planDir, checks, harnessRoot }): string, moved from bin/pi-implement with byte-identical text except lib/plan.ts becomes <harnessRoot>/lib/plan.ts. No other planner prompt changes.

preflight/PreflightInput accept optional testFiles?: string[] and pythonProject?: string | null. Recognized Python tests plus an explicit null project add exactly Python tests but no Python project; add .pi/pipeline.json with pythonProject. Preserve all existing checks/warnings and unchanged results when new fields are absent.

bin/pi-implement: derive real harness root from its own parent; parse --repo <path> as a value-bearing flag like --progress, excluding both values from spec-query discovery; default target lookup to process.cwd(). Usage gains [--repo <path>]; terminal use works from inside target or via --repo.
Runner targetRepo failure exits 2 with not inside a git repository: <path>. Missing target/docs/specs exits 2 naming docs/specs and the target, checked before spec resolution/preflight.

Use the target for spec resolution/text, .tests files, dirty status, branch/HEAD, review and detached worktrees, grading and final worktree removals. Never infer target from the runner file or require target to contain harness files.

Keep runner/settings/quota hold/lib imports and scripts/run-plan.mjs owned by the harness installation, using existing hermetic PI_BUILD_SETTINGS and PI_BUILD_QUOTA_HOLD semantics. Target-specific test config belongs to target; pi-build host default remains unchanged.

Runner computes pythonProject via pythonProjectFor and passes discovered target testFiles plus that value to preflight before any model call; missing Python projects block, while Node-only foreign targets may use null.

--dry-run preserves current spec/tests/plan/runRecord/checks/planner/editor/commands fields and stdout behaviour without progress, and adds real target, harnessRoot, runDir base and pythonProject. Foreign --repo and from-inside output must match; pi-build numeric query 15 resolves unchanged.
Use runDirBase for new runs and --resume lookup under the identical base; preserve pi-build's current unnamespaced run directory and resume metadata/worktree behaviour.
Runner invokes the shared object-argument planPrompt with harnessRoot, pointing a planner in any target worktree to the harness Plan contract.

Runner starts <harnessRoot>/scripts/run-plan.mjs, not the target worktree's copy, passing --repo <work> and --python-project <value> (empty string for null) and preserving plan/run-dir/progress/resume arguments and forwarding semantics.
Handoff restores/cleans .agent only when the worktree directory exists, and restores only when .agent has tracked files; absent or untracked-only .agent must not discard a finished run.

Wrap markImplemented and both index/spec writes. On failure emit notice index not updated: <reason>, append ## Index and that line to the run record, exclude spec and index from the handoff commit, and continue recording/reporting/committing/removing worktrees and handing off.

Preserve exit codes 0, 1, 2, 75, 130 and meanings, quota/resume instructions, abort retention, progress events, plan-only behaviour and all current pi-build behaviour except the specified harness-owned run-plan invocation.

Foreign-target runs never write target artifacts in pi-build's working tree. Run artifacts belong under the target or runRoot/<target-basename>; explicitly required harnessRoot dry-run metadata and harness executable/interface paths still identify the harness, not writable target state.

scripts/run-plan.mjs REPO is realpath of --repo when provided, otherwise its current location-derived default. All repository-relative validation, commits, plans, worktrees, typecheck and grading follow that target, including refusing run-dir inside it.

run-plan pythonProject is --python-project's value whenever the flag is present, including the empty string, otherwise the existing settings.pipeline.pythonProject || tools/map lookup. Do not use truthiness to discard the explicit empty value.

Preserve run-plan's models, grading, plan gate, continuation, quota behaviour and progress. Keep installation-owned lookups installation-owned when splitting REPO from harness, particularly the existing holdStatus bin/pi-continue lookup; audit existing resume diagnostics without changing protocol or adding commands.

pipelineExtension default async factory accepts options: { harnessRoot?: string } = {}; resolve harness once at load from override or findHarnessRoot(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); remove repositoryRoot entirely.
Tool per-call check order starts with no harness/missing harness/bin/pi-implement, yielding an error naming the harness or module file searched, before repository checks or spawn.
Tool next calls targetRepo(ctx.cwd); null returns implement_spec needs a git repository; <cwd> is not inside one. and does not start the runner.
Tool spawns the harness runner with implementArgs({ ...params, repo: target }), cwd target and testEnv(process.env), supporting sessions below the target root while preserving environment cleanup.

Every non-hand-off result, including missing runner/repo, exit 2/75/other failures, spawn errors, no handoff, plan-only and abort, isError true and text ends in newline + STOP_AND_REPORT; keep existing diagnostics and resume instructions before it. Hand-off text/result stays unchanged.

Tool explicitly declares exposure direct. Preserve its current description sentence and append If it fails: plus STOP_AND_REPORT. Put no stop instruction in a guideline, namespace instruction, system-prompt or other prompt field.

Preserve tool name/parameters/rendering, streaming updates before completion, cost/branch/run-record results and SIGTERM abort behaviour; successful handoffs are not errors and do not include STOP_AND_REPORT.

tests/pipeline-tool.test.ts changes in exactly three fixture places: git init -q root; pass { harnessRoot: root } to pipelineExtension; append --repo, fs.realpathSync(root) to expected args. All other assertions and fixture behaviour remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Update only README lines describing implement_spec/runner usage to cover arbitrary target repositories, terminal --repo, from-inside invocation, preserved branch handoff and resume; no unrelated documentation cleanup.

Update only agent/EXTENSIONS.md's pipeline-tool description to document harness/target ownership, direct exposure and tool-local failure reporting; preserve all extension coordination contracts and event ownership.

Run V1-V8 using the protected spec test command; run each Luna acceptance test; record commands, results and repair rounds. Tests are hermetic and make no model calls. Do not skip/weaken protected tests to pass.
V9: run tests/pipeline-tool.test.ts with only the three allowed edits and show its entire diff; show empty diffs for every other protected file.

V10: compare the complete failing-test set with step 0, allowing only fixed failures and the explicitly permitted transient §6.6 cases; include repository check baselines separately rather than claiming the failing offline doctor or map collection was fixed.

V11: either demonstrate absent-.agent/missing-index-row handoff via a written test, or explicitly report it not exercised and why. This plan chooses the report alternative: no handoff extraction/new exported interface and no paid model-driven end-to-end run; O5 implementation is still required and must be reviewed.

Verify real pi/jiti import.meta.url runner discovery after changes in a pi session, not only native Node tests. Record actual result or not-run with reason; never equate the override fixture with proof of the loader seam.

Report O1-O5 evidence and each §7 path actually run, distinguishing protected test coverage, child-trust command, unexercised handoff and deferred next real model-driven use. Explain all deviations, including installation-owned hold lookup and any invariant interpretation.

Apply §9 stop rules: at most three repair rounds per failed check group, stop on a protected-test error, scope growth, design-changing grounding contradiction or repeated failure without a new testable diagnosis. Never call unrun checks passed.
Commit locally on the branch started on; never push, alter remotes, create/delete remote branches, tags, PRs or releases, land main, or rewrite others' commits. Keep unrelated state out of commits.

Deliver §10 report: start revision/step-0 baseline and trust, V-check commands/output/status/repairs, O/path evidence, diff stat, protected-file diffs, complete changed functions with callers and deviations. Do not mark the spec implemented during planning or before actual acceptance; final status/index updates remain the successful pipeline handoff's responsibility.

tasks.brief: Stage 0 — retain the planner's pre-edit grounding and constraints in the report; do not rebaseline after Luna edits. This task is Sol because it reasons across the installed environment, runner, tool and test surfaces. Planning started at 3ff1666fa71d72ccadf238568fb83d5ef14e38da on the existing pipeline review branch with git status --short empty; /.agents/notes/index.md absent. Expected versus actual: extension repositoryRoot currently walks up for bin/pi-implement AND docs/specs and spawns there (matches); runner root/spec/status/branch/worktree are location-owned (matches); run-plan is started from work/scripts and sets location-owned REPO (matches); planner prompt refers to relative lib/plan.ts (matches); both Python defaults are tools/map (matches); spec regex/row matching are four-digit only (matches); .agent restore/clean are unconditional (matches); tool exposure unset (matches); PI_BUILD_SETTINGS and PI_BUILD_QUOTA_HOLD are supported (matches); existing fixture is not a git repo and asserts exact cwd/args (matches). The measured rows' code is present although this start revision is newer than the cited 4684f86. Installed pi --version is 1.2.0; deps.txt expects 0.99.1. No design-changing contradiction was found: do not fix installation/dependency versions or other baseline failures in this scope. The real pi/jiti import.meta.url row remains a required post-change runtime verification, not a planning pass. Before any implementation, planner ran env -u PI_BUILD_PIPELINE -u PI_BUILD_SUBAGENT_ROLE -u PI_BUILD_TELEMETRY_DB node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/*.test.ts: exit 0, 137 tests, 136 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (recorded measurement database unavailable). Therefore expected eight pre-existing failures is NOT reproduced; baseline Node failing set is empty. Original output: /tmp/spec18-start-suite-xZdrj4.tap. Additional checks: ./doctor.sh --offline exit 1 at 'pi version 1.2.0, deps.txt wants 0.99.1' (/tmp/spec18-baseline-offline-90g1ZK.log); ./doctor.sh --project . exit 0 (/tmp/spec18-baseline-project-twv2R2.log); uv run --project tools/map pytest -q exit 2 in collection, tests/fixtures/pipeline-smoke/SPEC-9001-add-smoke-double.tests/test_smoke_double.py imports missing map_build.smoke_double (/tmp/spec18-baseline-map-7pvNPZ.log). The protected SPEC-0018 tests currently exit 1, 19 tests/1 pass/18 fail (/tmp/spec18-contract-baseline-nhnFOi.tap); these are new-contract failures, NOT regressions in the existing Node baseline. Child-trust: created /tmp/spec18-trust-oVVday/repo outside pi-build, committed .pi/settings.json, added worktree /tmp/spec18-trust-oVVday/work, then from the worktree ran timeout 30s env -u PI_BUILD_PIPELINE -u PI_BUILD_SUBAGENT_ROLE -u PI_BUILD_TELEMETRY_DB pi --mode json --list-models. Exit 0 without blocking or prompting, no model call; stdout empty, stderr model listing. Logs /tmp/spec18-trust-oVVday/{stdout,stderr}.log retained; fixture/worktree removed. This is the exact cheap check allowed by §4, not proof of a model-driven child run. childPiArgs already supplies --approve. Record these findings, retain protected files and deferred items, do not edit sealed notes. The executor runs Luna tasks before Sol integration; the planner has already performed the pre-edit checks, and this task records that pre-edit evidence rather than pretending to execute before Luna. Planning gate evidence: countVerifyChecks returned 11; validatePlan returned { ok: true, errors: [] }; undeclaredImports returned [] for each Luna test. Running each acceptanceTest individually with node --experimental-strip-types --test --test-reporter=tap returned exit 1: spec-ids.test.ts had five behavioural failures and one unchanged-numeric regression pass; pipeline-decisions.test.ts failed module instantiation because the declared new STOP_AND_REPORT export is not implemented. The latter's behavioural assertions are present but could not execute before the new exports exist. No production or protected-test edits were made; no implementation repair rounds were used.

Stage 6.1 — extend only lib/specs.ts to alphanumeric spec identifiers. Read lib/specs.ts and docs/specs/SPEC-0018-run-implement-spec-from-any-repo.plan/spec-ids.test.ts; the latter is read-only. All decisions and interfaces are supplied here; do not inspect or change callers. Keep exported SpecRef { id: string; slug: string; file: string }, Resolution = { ok: true; spec: SpecRef } | { ok: false; error: string }, listSpecs(fileNames: string[]): SpecRef[], resolveSpec(fileNames: string[], query: string): Resolution, markImplemented(indexText: string, specText: string, id: string, by: string): { index: string; spec: string }, and specPaths(spec: SpecRef): { spec: string; tests: string; plan: string; runRecord: string }. Update the internal SPEC_FILE ID portion from four digits to [0-9A-Za-z]+; keep the SPEC- prefix, current lowercase slug grammar, .md ending, original ID spelling, localeCompare sorting and exclusion of slug run. Correct the stale four-digits comment on SpecRef.id. Resolve IDs case-insensitively, including case-insensitive SPEC- prefix, bare/prefixed IDs, filename/path (with optional .md) and slug; trim query and strip path just as today. Keep digits-only lengths 1 through 4 zero-padded to length 4 (including currently supported SPEC-7), while longer numeric and alphanumeric IDs compare directly. Preserve current extraction of an ID from a spec-shaped filename even when the supplied slug differs. Hits must be filtered as a set of specs, not concatenated duplicates for overlapping query forms. More than one hit returns the existing '"<query>" matches more than one spec: <hit IDs>' form naming all hits; case-folded duplicates must not select the first one. Unknown errors retain 'No spec "<query>". Specs: <id slug list or none>'. Do not change slug case semantics, error prefixes or unrelated query behaviour. markImplemented matches exactly one row whose first trimmed cell matches ^[0-9A-Za-z]+$ and equals the supplied id case-insensitively. Preserve the 'Expected exactly one index row for <id>' throw, replace only that row's status/by cells and the first header Status cell, preserving whitespace, other rows and no-header behaviour. specPaths must remain identical, including runRecord SPEC-<id>-run.md. Do not export SPEC_FILE or add exports. Forbidden edits: every other file, bin/pi-rework, all existing tests, the spec's .tests directory, this acceptance test, plan.json, docs/index, prompts, settings, notes and router wiring. No cross-file adaptation is your responsibility. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test docs/specs/SPEC-0018-run-implement-spec-from-any-repo.plan/spec-ids.test.ts; do not implement other stages.

Stage 6.2 — implement only the specified pure/shared decisions in lib/pipeline.ts. Read lib/pipeline.ts and docs/specs/SPEC-0018-run-implement-spec-from-any-repo.plan/pipeline-decisions.test.ts (read-only). Existing countVerifyChecks import/use remains unchanged; no other source file needs modification or caller inspection. Exact exports: STOP_AND_REPORT = 'Do not implement this spec with other tools. Report this result to the user and wait for instructions.'; findHarnessRoot(fromPath: string): string | null; targetRepo(cwd: string): string | null; implementArgs(input: { spec: string; planOnly?: boolean; resume?: boolean; repo?: string }): string[]; pythonProjectFor(input: { target: string; harnessRoot: string; settings: unknown }): string | null; runDirBase(input: { runRoot: string; target: string; harnessRoot: string; id: string; slug: string }): string; planPrompt(input: { spec: string; planDir: string; checks: number; harnessRoot: string }): string. Extend existing PreflightInput with testFiles?: string[] and pythonProject?: string | null, preserving preflight(input: PreflightInput): Preflight and every other export unchanged. findHarnessRoot realpaths its input first, uses stat to choose directory versus file parent, walks to nearest ancestor containing bin/pi-implement, returns that ancestor's realpath; catch any error and return null, including nonexistent inputs; directory/file symlinks work; no docs/specs requirement. targetRepo runs git -C cwd rev-parse --show-toplevel and realpaths trimmed stdout, returning null without throwing on git/realpath errors. implementArgs keeps exact current argument order and appends --repo, repo when provided after --resume; absent repo leaves output unchanged. pythonProjectFor precedence: read <target>/.pi/pipeline.json and use pythonProject if a nonempty string, returned unchanged/relative (ignore unusable/missing config); otherwise same-real-path target/harness returns nonempty string settings.pipeline.pythonProject or 'tools/map'; otherwise target/pyproject.toml existence returns '.'; else null. Do not use the host setting for foreign targets. Shared identity comparison realpaths existing target/harness paths (so symlink aliases compare equal) and falls back to resolved lexical paths when realpath is impossible: required because runDirBase's protected tests also pass nonexistent /src/pi-build paths. runDirBase returns join(runRoot, 'SPEC-' + id + '-' + slug) for same identity, otherwise join(runRoot, basename(target), 'SPEC-' + id + '-' + slug). Preserve input ID/slug spelling. preflight adds exactly 'Python tests but no Python project; add .pi/pipeline.json with pythonProject' to blocking when pythonProject === null AND (testFiles ?? []) contains a match for the existing PY_TEST regex /(?:^|\/)(?:test_[^/]*|[^/]*_test)\.py$/. No blocking for unspecified fields, Node-only/unrecognized files or non-null project. Keep all existing preflight checks/messages/order/warnings intact, and reuse the existing pattern rather than broadening recognition. planPrompt must return exactly the following template with only the displayed placeholders interpolated: Read ${spec} and the repository. Write an implementation plan to ${planDir}/plan.json following the Plan interface in ${harnessRoot}/lib/plan.ts, and one acceptance test per Luna task in ${planDir}/.

Map each verification V-number, 1 through ${checks}, to verifyMap key without the V (V3 is key "3"). Order tasks by the spec's stages. List every requirement and map every V-number to requirement ids or "process". Split tasks into one file each; assign to Luna only tasks needing no cross-file reasoning or open design decision; assign the rest to Sol. Each Luna brief must stand alone, with exact interfaces, constants, reading and forbidden edits. Tests import only declared interfaces and assert behaviour. Run validatePlan and undeclaredImports, confirm every acceptance test fails before implementation. Do not implement anything. There is no trailing newline. Use node:fs/path/child_process as needed, no new package, no new exported input types. Existing childPiArgs, testEnv, costByRole, childEnv, pipelineRunRoot, pipelineTelemetryDbs, Command, testCommands, PreflightInput and Preflight remain compatible. Forbidden edits: every other file (including bin/pi-implement's old planPrompt; Sol removes it), all tests/specs/plan files, prompts/guidelines, settings, notes and router. Do not adapt callers or implement later stages. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test docs/specs/SPEC-0018-run-implement-spec-from-any-repo.plan/pipeline-decisions.test.ts.

Stage 6.3 — integrate harness and target roots in bin/pi-implement only. Sol owns this because CLI parsing, imports, library decisions, two worktrees, grading and the final commit/handoff must agree across files. Read §6.3, lib/pipeline.ts and lib/specs.ts, scripts/run-plan.mjs argument handling, and protected runner.test.ts; do not edit their contracts here. Import the new targetRepo, pythonProjectFor, runDirBase and planPrompt helpers; remove the local planPrompt, preserving its moved text exactly. Realpath the runner and derive harnessRoot from its own parent, not cwd or target. Parse --repo as a value flag alongside --progress, rejecting a missing value and never taking flag values as the query; preserve old switches/usage with [--repo <path>] added. Resolve targetRepo(repo flag or process.cwd()); exact nonrepo exit-2 diagnostic, and target/docs/specs existence diagnostic before resolution/preflight. Every current root-based target read/git operation must use target: spec/tests/status/HEAD/review branch/worktrees and both removals. Keep lib imports/settings/quota and executable lookup installation-owned. Determine settings/pythonProject early enough to give preflight testFiles/pythonProject and to refuse Python tests before models. Retain current dirty warnings. Compute base with runDirBase for dry run, fresh run and resume; include target/harnessRoot/runDir/pythonProject in dry-run JSON while keeping all existing fields and stdout/progress handling. Use shared object-argument planPrompt. Start harnessRoot/scripts/run-plan.mjs with --repo work and --python-project (pythonProject ?? ''), preserving plan/run-dir/progress/resume args and child cwd/worktree, events and exit semantics. Handoff keeps complete record/report even on index failures: skip .agent cleanup if directory absent, restore only if git ls-files -- .agent has tracked files, and clean only existing directory. Wrap index/spec reads, markImplemented and both writes; only on full success add those two paths to git add. On any throw emit notice 'index not updated: <reason>', append '
## Index

index not updated: <reason>
' to the written run record, leave spec/index unstaged by this commit, then continue the report/run-record commit and both target worktree removals. Consider a partial first write when the second throws; do not accidentally stage either path on fallback. Do not introduce a new extraction/export just for a handoff test: the plan deliberately uses V11's permitted explicit not-exercised report, and makes no paid model calls. Preserve plan-only, resume metadata, abort retention, quota/hold behaviour and all five exit codes. A foreign target must not require its own scripts/lib/bin/.agent or write in the harness working tree. Explicit harnessRoot metadata is installation identity, not a target artifact; record that interpretation of §8's printed-path invariant. Run the protected runner tests and pi-build dry-run regression with hermetic settings/hold paths. Do not edit protected tests or the fixture in this task.

Stage 6.4 — integrate run-plan's target/installation split in scripts/run-plan.mjs only. Sol is required: the flags are supplied by bin/pi-implement and REPO currently also controls holdStatus's bin/pi-continue installation lookup, so blindly replacing a constant is insufficient cross-file reasoning. Read §6.4, the edited runner invocation, existing argValue/readSettings/holdStatus/resumeCommand/ensureWorktree and the protected runner.test.ts. Set repository REPO to realpath(--repo value) when that flag is present, else retain the current location-derived default; retain a separate location-derived harness identity for installation-owned executable lookups, notably bin/pi-continue. Preserve existing quota decisions rather than silently losing hold checks in foreign repositories. Select pythonProject by presence of --python-project, not truthiness, taking its value verbatim including ''; absent flag keeps settings.pipeline?.pythonProject || 'tools/map'. Verify all target-relative plan containment/run-dir containment, showFile/git/worktrees, spec/plan tests and typecheck use REPO and no harness working-tree writes occur. Keep the direct-invocation default compatible. Audit resume diagnostics for replayable target flags without changing progress protocol/quota semantics; document any necessary scoped adjustment rather than changing unrelated behaviour. Preserve models, thinking, battery, integration, retry/continuation and gate logic. The O1 ownership contract requires the harness bin/pi-continue lookup even though §6.4 describes the REPO replacement tersely; report the previously implicit seam in §10, and stop if scope genuinely must grow. Run protected runner.test.ts including its run-dir-inside-target refusal and tests/run-plan-thinking.test.ts. No edits to other files or protected tests.

Stage 6.5 — integrate the tool in extensions/pipeline.ts only. This is Sol because extension-loader identity, the runner's new CLI, target discovery and all progress/abort/error outcomes must agree; do not route it to Luna. Read §6.5, lib/pipeline.ts exports, current execute/result/render logic, protected tool.test.ts and relevant installed pi extension docs. Default export remains async pipelineExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI, options: { harnessRoot?: string } = {}): Promise<void>. Resolve harness once when factory loads, options.harnessRoot ?? findHarnessRoot(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); remove repositoryRoot and obsolete imports. Per execute: first no harness or absent bin/pi-implement -> error identifying harness path or module file; then targetRepo(ctx.cwd) null -> exact 'implement_spec needs a git repository; <cwd> is not inside one.'; otherwise spawn harness/bin/pi-implement with implementArgs({ ...params, repo: target }), cwd target and existing testEnv(process.env). Every path except a genuine successful branch handoff must be isError true, ending with exactly '
' + STOP_AND_REPORT after existing text (include early errors, spawn failure, no done/branch, exits 1/2/75/130, abort and plan-only). Preserve current hold/preflight/abort detail, resume: true hints, updates and handoff predicate. Successful handoff result unchanged and contains no stop sentence. Explicit exposure: 'direct'; description is its existing full sentence plus ' If it fails: ' + STOP_AND_REPORT. Do not add guideline/system/namespace/prompt fields or change event registration, model choice, schemas, protocol or rendering. Protected tool.test.ts checks fake override and native no-override discovery; final integration must separately report real pi/jiti seam verification. Existing pipeline-tool.test.ts is expected to need only the later three fixture adaptations. Do not edit it here.

Stage 6.6 — adapt tests/pipeline-tool.test.ts in exactly the three places authorized by the spec. Sol owns this protected-test exception because it must check the new cross-file contract and show its entire diff. execFileSync is already imported: add execFileSync('git', ['init', '-q', root]) in fixture setup; pass { harnessRoot: root } as the second argument to pipelineExtension; extend the success invocation expectation's args after --resume with '--repo', fs.realpathSync(root). No fourth change, assertion relaxation, formatting cleanup, type change, new helper, abort assertion change or new suffix assertion. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/pipeline-tool.test.ts; all three existing cases must pass with streaming/env/cost/abort behaviour intact. Show git diff -- tests/pipeline-tool.test.ts and verify every other existing/protected test diff is empty. This task changes no source file.

Documentation stage after §6 — edit only README.md lines describing pipeline/tool usage. Sol checks this against the implemented CLI/tool rather than asking Luna to infer cross-file behaviour. Explain that implement_spec works from anywhere within a git repository with docs/specs and its spec .tests, uses installed pi-build as harness, and terminal users can invoke the harness bin/pi-implement <spec> --repo <target> or run that executable from inside the target without --repo; retain --dry-run and --resume examples with meaningful harness invocation and preserved branch review/handoff. Do not imply target contains bin/pi-implement, auto-merge/main landing or absence of required spec tests. Do not add stop-and-report instructions outside tool description/results. No unrelated README edits.

Documentation stage — edit only agent/EXTENSIONS.md's Pipeline tool subsection. Sol verifies the prose against extension and runner contracts. State explicit direct exposure, installation-owned harness runner versus session git target and tool-local error reporting. Preserve 'subscribes to no events' and all other extension ownership/invalidation contracts. Do not paste STOP_AND_REPORT into guidelines, instructions or system-prompt contracts; descriptive documentation is not a second behavioural instruction. Do not edit unrelated sections or add another extension.

Final verification/§10 report — Sol integrates all evidence, without expanding a task into a new production file. Extend the baseline report from S00 and deliver the same report at the external run report path requested by the integration runner (the outer runner copies it to this repo path at handoff).
